newsitem.title: POLAND: Anti-rightists and nationalists scrap in Warsaw.
newsitem.headline: Anti-rightists and nationalists scrap in Warsaw.

text.p: Small groups of radical nationalists and anti-rightists scrapped in central Warsaw on Monday, Poland's national day, public television reported.

The television said the nationalists marched to the city's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in a protest against Poland's plans to join the European Union and against the current government led by ex-communists.
As anarchist-led counter-protesters scuffled with police, the nationalists reached the tomb. But after their ceremony the factions skirmished after dark in nearby streets.
A Warsaw police duty officer told Reuters an estimated 200 nationalists and about 1,000 of their opponents had been involved, adding that four people had been detained.
While most Poles across the mainstream political spectrum back EU membership, parts of the radical right say it will damage Poland's sovereignty.
